title: Sell Mineral Rights in Pecos, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Pecos, TX | Reeves County Buyer
metaDescription: Pecos sits at the center of the busiest stretch of the Delaware Basin. Get a candid valuation on your Reeves County mineral or royalty interest.
heroLead: Pecos is the seat of Reeves County and about as close to the center of current Delaware Basin drilling as any town gets.
intro: Drive into Pecos from any direction and you'll pass frac spreads, water disposal facilities, and man-camp housing that wasn't there fifteen years ago. This town has been an oil town since the early days of the Permian, but the scale of what's happening around it now is different from anything in its earlier history, and that's reshaped what mineral ownership here is worth.

sections.heading: Stacked pay right under town and around it
paragraphs: Acreage in and around Pecos commonly produces from multiple formations — Wolfcamp, Bone Spring, sometimes Avalon shale — stacked on top of each other under the same surface footprint. If your family's minerals are anywhere near town, it's worth checking whether your interest is pooled into more than one spacing unit, since that's common here and changes how your royalty adds up across separate checks.

sections.heading: The Pecos River and old town-adjacent leases
paragraphs: Some of the oldest leases in this part of Texas run through land along the Pecos River corridor, tied to allotments and ranching-family holdings that predate the current horizontal boom by decades. If your interest traces back to one of those older leases, held by production through the years, a new operator picking up the acreage for horizontal development can suddenly make that old paper worth far more than the family ever expected.

faqs.question: Why do I get more than one royalty check for what I thought was a single mineral interest near Pecos?
faqs.answer: Multiple formations are often developed separately under the same acreage here, each with its own spacing unit and operator. We look at all of your units together when valuing your overall interest.

faqs.question: Is Pecos still seeing a lot of new wells, or has activity leveled off?
faqs.answer: It remains one of the most actively permitted areas of the Delaware Basin, though pace varies block by block. We check current activity on your specific tract before quoting anything.

faqs.question: My family's lease near Pecos is decades old. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can help. Older leases that have been continuously held by production remain valid, and if new horizontal development picks up the same acreage, that old paper can suddenly be worth considerably more than it was when it was signed.
